title: ContextLedgerEvidenceEntry
description: One hash-chained ledger record describing ONE source observation of ONE content-addressed evidence blob. PERSISTENCE SHAPE IS PART OF THE CONTRACT: each entry is written as its own immutable file (ledger-entries/entry-NNNNNN.json) on the WriteOnce vault -- never appended into a shared file, which would be incompatible with WORM auto-lock and would leave historical proof mutable. The mutable head pointer lives on the normal metadata share and is an optimisation, not an authority: if lost, the head is rebuilt by scanning entries and following prevHash/entryHash. Invariant: historical evidence and historical proof are immutable; only operational state is mutable.

seq.description: ORDERING ASSISTANCE ONLY -- never identity, never authority. The identity of an entry is entryHash; the truth of history is the prevHash/entryHash chain. seq exists so humans and queries can order entries cheaply. Never resolve an entry by seq, never assume seq is gap-free, and never treat a seq collision as meaningful -- resolve by entryHash and walk the chain.

prevHash.description: entryHash of seq-1. Null only at seq 0 (genesis).

entryHash.description: sha256(canonicalJson(entry without entryHash) + prevHash). Makes the ledger tamper-evident.

evidenceId.description: Deterministic id derived from (sourceSystem, sourceNativeId, contentHash). Identifies THIS OBSERVATION, not the blob.

contentHash.description: Address of the immutable blob. Two observations of identical bytes share this value and MUST NOT produce two canonical blobs.

sourceNativeId.description: The source's own identifier -- sessionId, message uuid, composerId, commit SHA. Never invented by us.

sourceObservation.description: Where this particular observation was seen. Distinguishes the WSL corpus from the Windows mirror when both contain identical bytes.

sourceTimestamp.description: When the original event happened. Null when the source does not expose it (Cursor WSL transcripts).

repoBinding.description: All nullable -- absent binding is MISSING, never guessed.

storageLocator.description: Fan-out is INDEPENDENT from the spool to each target. The backup leg must never be derived from, or depend on, the primary.

spoolPath.description: WSL ext4 write-ahead spool. Null only after FULLY_PROTECTED cleanup.

backup.description: Independent recovery copy. NOT an authority. Has its own manifests and verification history.

durabilityState.description: Fan-out durability. The spool copy is NOT eligible for cleanup until FULLY_PROTECTED, which requires plaintextHash == primary verified hash == backup verified hash. Reaching only PRIMARY_VERIFIED never authorises spool deletion -- that is the whole point of keeping the local copy. INTEGRITY_INCIDENT is terminal until a human resolves it.

durabilityProof.description: Three independent hashes. Equality across all three is the only thing that authorises FULLY_PROTECTED.

primaryHash.description: Re-hashed ON the Synology, not predicted locally.

backupHash.description: Re-hashed ON wesleydesk, independently of the primary leg.

lastScrubAt.description: Periodic integrity scrub: ledger hash vs primary vs backup.

lastRestoreProofAt.description: A backup is proven by RECONSTRUCTION, not by files existing. Records the last real restore from the backup copy.

ciphertextHashesIdentical.description: ciphertextHash(primary) == ciphertextHash(backup). The encrypted bytes must be identical at both destinations.

provenanceClass.description: Raw capture is never promoted above DISCOVERED by the capture path.

captureCompleteness.description: Absent data is MISSING, never zero.

supersededBy.description: evidenceId that supersedes this observation. Supersession is an edge, never a deletion.

continuationOf.description: Session stitching across restarts or hosts.

encryption.description: Evidence is encrypted in WSL BEFORE either storage target receives it. Neither drive is trusted to provide confidentiality, and DSM share encryption is currently DISABLED anyway.

algorithm.description: e.g. AES-256-GCM. Authenticated encryption required -- a plain stream cipher gives no tamper detection.

keyRef.description: NAME of the key in the approved secret system (Doppler). NEVER the key material, and never a path on either drive.

keyVersion.description: Key rotation identity. Old evidence must stay decryptable after rotation.

plaintextHash.description: Identity and dedup hash. Two observations of identical plaintext share one canonical object.

ciphertextHash.description: What remote re-hash compares against. Encryption must be deterministic per object, or the stored bytes are re-hashed after write rather than predicted.

propagationPolicy.description: The backup is append-only and must never obediently reproduce a mistake made on the primary.

deletesPropagate.description: MUST be false. A delete on the Synology is never mirrored to the backup.

modificationsPropagate.description: MUST be false. Objects are content-addressed and append-only.

persistence.description: Where and how this entry is stored. Enforces the immutable-per-entry shape.

entryFile.description: Immutable path, written once, never reopened. Prefer deriving the filename from entryHash rather than seq: a content-derived name cannot collide, whereas two writers independently computing seq+1 would collide and rely on the storage layer refusing an overwrite -- an accident of WORM rather than a designed guarantee.

storageClass.description: Ledger entries live on the WriteOnce vault alongside blobs, manifests and receipts.

batchManifest.description: Immutable per-batch manifest, e.g. immutable-metadata/manifests/{batchId}.json. Never an extended file.

headPointerIsAuthority.description: MUST be false. The chain is the authority; the head pointer is a cache.

chainIntegrity.description: Concurrency contract for the append primitive. Locked before a second adapter exists, because two writers silently claiming the same predecessor forks history in a way that is only discoverable after the evidence needed to diagnose it is already wrong.

headTransition.description: The head pointer MUST advance by compare-and-swap: the write succeeds only if the current head still equals expectedPrevHash. A losing writer re-reads the head and retries against the new predecessor. Appending without CAS is a contract violation even if it appears to work under a single worker.

expectedPrevHash.description: The head this writer observed. The CAS compares against this. Null only for genesis.

seqAssignedUnderCas.description: True when seq was allocated by the winner inside the CAS, which is what keeps numbering unique without making it authoritative.

forkDetected.description: Two entries claiming the same prevHash is a FORK. It is an INTEGRITY_INCIDENT, never auto-merged and never resolved by preferring a seq or a timestamp -- both branches are preserved for a human.

casRetries.description: Retries before winning the head. Non-zero is normal under concurrency; sustained growth indicates contention worth investigating.
